narrative.overview:
NMTK is a suite where complexity is accessible on demand at every level, not necessarily always visible. The user sees a calm, controlled workspace. Behind that surface, pipeline state, hardware diagnostics, and process telemetry are always one interaction away. The interface holds information in readiness; it does not broadcast it.

The suite occupies a precise space between scientific instrument and modern professional tool. It has the visual discipline of precision equipment without the aesthetic of a developer IDE, an enterprise console, or a consumer application. It is technically honest and visually composed.

NMTK presents two symmetrical themes: dark navy and light silver-blue. Three workbench modes (command, studio, instrument) share one family identity but carry distinct palette accents.
keyCharacteristics: State accessible on demand, not broadcast: depth one interaction away, calm at surface
Three workbench modes with distinct palette accents within one shared shape and type language
Dense without cramped: hierarchy is clear, surfaces breathe, labels are readable at 12px
Operationally honest: every status color has exactly one meaning, never used decoratively
No ornamentation: every element earns its place or is removed

rules.name: The Semantic Purity Rule
rules.body: Status colors have one job each: communicating operational state. They are never used for decoration, emphasis, or branding.

rules.name: The Mode Palette Rule
rules.body: Command blue, studio violet, and instrument cyan are applied only to their assigned modules. Chrome tinting follows mode assignment strictly. These assignments never cross.

rules.name: The No-Oversize Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight contrast before scale. 28px is the ceiling. This is a professional workstation; it earns authority through precision, not scale.

rules.name: The Mono Boundary Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for machine-generated content, user-authored code, and numeric telemetry. Navigation labels and status text always use Space Grotesk.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. State changes produce tint shifts or border accents, not shadow introduction.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Cards use a 1px border to define their bounds. If an element needs to feel elevated, lighten its background by one tonal step. Do not add a shadow.

rules.name: The No-Nested-Cards Rule
rules.body: A card inside a card is always wrong. Use tonal sections, inline rows, or subtle-border dividers for internal hierarchy.

rules.name: The Inline-Over-Modal Rule
rules.body: Modals are for blocking decisions only. Diagnostic detail, log output, and progressive disclosure use the utility panel or inline expansion.

dos: Apply mode palettes strictly: command blue for shell and Neurohub, studio violet for neurocnl and Neurosim, instrument cyan/teal for Neurosense, Neurochip, and Neurobench.
Use tonal depth (background tint steps) rather than shadows to communicate surface hierarchy.
Achieve typographic hierarchy through Space Grotesk weight contrast (w400 vs w700) before reaching for size differences.
Map every status indicator to one of the six semantic states: healthy, running, degraded, warning, error, live.
Make state accessible on demand: summary at surface, detail one interaction away.
Keep the top app bar at 52px and the workspace bar at 48px.
Use the pulsing status dot exclusively for degraded and error states.
Use JetBrains Mono for all code, CNL text, and column-aligned numeric telemetry; never for chrome.
donts: Don't let NMTK feel like a consumer SaaS (Canva, Wix): no marketing chrome, growth funnels, freemium onboarding wizards, or pastel animations.
Don't let it feel like an Arduino IDE: no clunky, cramped, dated developer-tool aesthetic.
Don't let it feel like a dark hacker terminal: no neon-on-black, no all-dark intimidation aesthetic.
Don't let it feel like SAP, Salesforce, or Atlassian Jira: no grey form overload, no bureaucratic navigation chrome, no ticket-board framing.
Don't let it feel like ZBrush or Blender: no toolbar overload, not every control visible at once.
Don't let it feel like VS Code: NMTK is a workstation, not an editor with extensions.
Don't use side-stripe borders: border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent on any card, list item, or callout.
Don't animate layout properties (width, height, padding, margin). Animate opacity and transform only.
Don't flood the surface with detail state. Surface status is a summary.
Don't reach for a modal first.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient).
